statement: Irreversible operations (production deploys, force-push, DB destruction or reset, secrets modification) require explicit human approval before execution. Read-only, reversible, or local-only operations are outside this scope.
Completion claims must be backed by executed verification (tests run, runtime checks, measurements). A successful build alone is not evidence of working software.
Secrets (API keys, passwords, tokens) must never be hardcoded in source code, committed to a repository, or printed to logs.
Changes reach protected branches (main, master, develop) only through pull requests. Direct commits or direct pushes to protected branches are forbidden.
Tool, model, or configuration changes are adopted only after measurement against pre-registered criteria, and re-measured when the environment or model generation changes.
Assertions about current system state (something is missing, broken, impossible, or dead) must be based on freshly executed checks, not on memory or assumption.
A discovered issue or improvement counts as real only after repeated reproduction (N-of-N in a fresh environment). A single occurrence is treated as flaky, not as a conclusion.
Each version explicitly defines what it will NOT do. Features beyond the current explicit goal (multi-tenant, billing, marketplaces, full dashboards) move to the roadmap instead of the current build.
Externally sourced or upstream-derived content must be labeled with its origin. First-person claims are reserved for directly experienced events; observed third-party cases must cite their source.
When uncommitted user work is present in a working tree, destructive git operations (reset --hard, checkout -f, clean -fd, stash drop) are forbidden without explicit user direction.
